supports.excerpt:
In some cases adding content dynamically is an important part of user experience. For example, when loading more products to a list of items or when updating live feed content. There are several ways to avoid unexpected layout shifts in those cases:

- Replace the old content with the new content within a fixed size container or use a carousel and remove the old content after the transition. Remember to disable any links and controls until the transition has completed to prevent accidental clicks or taps while the new content is coming in.

- Have the user initiate the load of new content, so they are not surprised by the shift (for example with a "Load more" or "Refresh" button). It's recommended to prefetch the content before the user interaction so that it shows up immediately. As a reminder, layout shifts that occur within 500 milliseconds of user input are not counted towards CLS.

- Seamlessly load the content offscreen and overlay a notice to the user that it's available (for example, with a "Scroll to top" button).

Examples of dynamic content loading without causing unexpected layout shifts. Left: Live feed content loading on Twitter. Right: "Load More" example on Chloé website. Check out how the YNAP team optimized for CLS when loading more content.

skill_drafts.name: Dynamic Content Loading with Layout Stability
skill_drafts.description: Prevent cumulative layout shift (CLS) when dynamically inserting new content by using fixed-size containers, carousels, or user-initiated loading patterns. Ensures visual stability during content updates.
skill_drafts.objective: Load new content dynamically without causing unexpected layout shifts
applicable_signals: User scrolls to end of list
New content is ready to be inserted
contraindications: Layout is already fixed and cannot shift
User has not initiated or consented to content load
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Choose loading strategy', 'detail': 'Select one of three approaches: fixed-size container/carousel, user-initiated load, or offscreen load with overlay notice'}

{'step': 2, 'action': 'Prepare container or trigger', 'detail': 'If using fixed-size container, ensure dimensions are set. If user-initiated, create button and prefetch content. If offscreen, prepare overlay notice.'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Disable interactive elements', 'detail': 'Disable links and controls during content transition to prevent accidental interaction'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Insert or transition content', 'detail': 'Replace old content with new content, or load offscreen and show notice to user'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Re-enable interactive elements', 'detail': 'After transition completes, re-enable links and controls'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Verify layout stability', 'detail': 'Confirm no unexpected layout shift occurred and CLS metric remains below threshold'}
triggers: Adding products to a list dynamically
Inserting new content after user interaction
constraints: Disable links and controls until transition completes to prevent accidental clicks
Layout shifts within 500 milliseconds of user input are not counted toward CLS
Content must be prefetched before user interaction when using user-initiated loading
cautions: Accidental clicks during transition can degrade user experience; disable controls until transition completes
Prefetching must occur before user interaction to ensure immediate display and avoid perceived delay
Offscreen loading with overlay notice may require user action to view new content; ensure notice is clear and accessible
output_contract: New content appears without visual shift; CLS metric remains below threshold; user interaction remains responsive; no layout reflow occurs outside the designated container or transition window

examples.input: User clicks 'Load more' button on product list
examples.output: New products load within fixed-size container; old products removed after transition; CLS does not increase
examples.notes: User-initiated load with prefetch ensures immediate display and no surprise shift

examples.input: Live feed updates with new posts
examples.output: New posts load offscreen; 'Scroll to top' notice appears; user can choose to view new content
examples.notes: Offscreen loading prevents unexpected layout shift; user controls when to view new content

metadata.prompt: When adding content dynamically (e.g., loading more products, updating live feeds), apply one of these approaches: (1) Replace old content with new content within a fixed-size container or carousel, disabling controls until transition completes; (2) Have the user initiate the load via a button (e.g., 'Load more'), prefetching content to show immediately; or (3) Load content offscreen and overlay a notice (e.g., 'Scroll to top' button). Ensure layout shifts do not occur unexpectedly.

Reduce CLS by ensuring pages are eligible for the bfcache

skill_drafts.name: Disable Controls During Content Transition
skill_drafts.description: Prevent accidental user interaction by disabling links and controls while new content is being inserted or transitioned. Re-enable after transition completes.
skill_drafts.objective: Block unintended user input during content replacement or carousel transitions
contraindications: Transition is instantaneous with no animation duration
User input is required during the content change
Content is not being replaced or updated
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify all interactive elements (links, buttons, form controls) in the transition zone', 'detail': 'Query or maintain a list of elements that could receive user input'}

{'step': 2, 'action': 'Set disabled state on all identified elements before transition starts', 'detail': 'Apply disabled attribute, aria-disabled, or pointer-events: none; optionally add visual feedback (reduced opacity, disabled cursor)'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Trigger content replacement or carousel animation', 'detail': 'Begin the transition (swap content, animate carousel, load new items)'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Wait for transition completion', 'detail': 'Listen for transitionend, animationend, or explicit completion callback'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Re-enable all interactive elements', 'detail': 'Remove disabled attribute, aria-disabled, or pointer-events restriction; restore visual state'}
triggers: Content replacement begins in a fixed-size container
New content is loading into the viewport
constraints: All interactive elements must be identified and tracked before disabling
Disable state must be applied atomically to prevent partial interaction
Re-enable must occur only after transition completion is confirmed
cautions: Ensure disabled state is visually communicated to users (e.g., opacity, cursor change)
Do not disable elements longer than necessary; re-enable promptly after transition
Test on touch devices to confirm tap events are blocked
output_contract: All interactive elements are disabled during transition; no accidental clicks or taps are registered; controls are re-enabled after transition completes and are fully functional.

examples.input: User clicks 'Load More' button; carousel begins sliding to show new products
examples.output: All product links and buttons in carousel are disabled during slide animation; re-enabled when slide completes
examples.notes: Prevents user from clicking a product link while the carousel is still moving

examples.input: Live feed updates with new posts; old posts fade out and new posts fade in
examples.output: All post interaction elements (like, reply, share buttons) are disabled during fade transition; re-enabled when fade completes
examples.notes: Prevents accidental interaction with partially-visible or transitioning content

metadata.prompt: When replacing old content with new content in a fixed-size container or carousel, disable all interactive elements (links, buttons, controls) before the transition begins. Keep them disabled until the transition animation or content insertion is complete, then re-enable them. This prevents accidental clicks or taps while new content is arriving.

skill_drafts.name: Prefetch Content Before User Interaction
skill_drafts.description: Load new content in the background before the user initiates a load action, so it displays immediately when requested without perceived delay or layout shift penalty.
skill_drafts.objective: Reduce perceived latency and eliminate layout shifts by preloading content before user-triggered load events
applicable_signals: Predictable content patterns (e.g., pagination, feed updates)
User interaction event listeners are registered
contraindications: Content is unpredictable or cannot be anticipated
Bandwidth is severely constrained or metered
User has disabled prefetch or background loading in browser settings
Network conditions are poor or unreliable
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify user-initiated load trigger points', 'detail': "Detect buttons, links, or controls that initiate content loading (e.g., 'Load more', 'Refresh')"}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Initiate background prefetch before user interaction', 'detail': 'Fetch and cache the next batch of content in the background using fetch, XMLHttpRequest, or service worker'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Store prefetched content in accessible cache', 'detail': 'Place content in memory, IndexedDB, or service worker cache for immediate retrieval'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Display content immediately upon user interaction', 'detail': 'When user clicks the load button, retrieve cached content and render without network delay'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Verify no layout shift occurs', 'detail': 'Confirm that content insertion does not cause unexpected layout shifts; use fixed containers or carousels if needed'}
triggers: User-initiated load button or refresh action is present in the interface
Content to be loaded can be predicted or anticipated
Load action is expected within a predictable timeframe
constraints: Prefetch must complete before user interaction to provide instantaneous display
Content must be stored in memory or cache accessible to the rendering engine
Prefetch should not block or delay other critical page operations
cautions: Prefetching unused content wastes bandwidth; only prefetch when user interaction is highly likely
Monitor cache size to avoid memory exhaustion on resource-constrained devices
Ensure prefetched content remains valid and does not become stale before user interaction
output_contract: Content is available in memory or cache before user interaction; load appears instantaneous (no perceived delay); layout shifts within 500 milliseconds of user input are not counted toward CLS; user experiences seamless content update without visual jank.

examples.input: User hovers over or focuses on a 'Load more' button; next page of products is predictable
examples.output: Next batch of product data is prefetched and cached; when user clicks 'Load more', products appear immediately without network latency
examples.notes: Prefetch triggered on hover or focus to maximize time before click

examples.input: Live feed with 'Refresh' button; new feed items can be anticipated
examples.output: New feed content is fetched in background before user clicks 'Refresh'; clicking 'Refresh' displays cached content instantly
examples.notes: Similar to Twitter live feed pattern mentioned in source

metadata.prompt: When a user-initiated load action (such as clicking 'Load more' or 'Refresh') is anticipated, prefetch the content in the background before the user interaction occurs. This ensures the content is available in memory or cache and can be displayed instantaneously upon user request. Layout shifts occurring within 500 milliseconds of user input are not counted toward CLS, but prefetching eliminates the shift entirely by having content ready.

skill_drafts.name: Offscreen Content Loading with User Notification
skill_drafts.description: Load new content outside the visible viewport and notify the user that it is available, avoiding unexpected layout shifts in the current view. Commonly used for live feed updates or additional product listings where the user should control when to view new content.
skill_drafts.objective: Insert content seamlessly without disrupting the current viewport layout
applicable_signals: Dynamic content arrival (live feed, product list expansion)
User is actively viewing current content
New content is ready but not yet needed in viewport
contraindications: Content must be immediately visible to the user
User is not expected to navigate to new content
Viewport space is severely limited and offscreen placement is not feasible
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Prepare new content in an offscreen container', 'detail': 'Create a DOM element or container positioned outside the visible viewport (e.g., using CSS `position: absolute; top: -9999px` or similar)'}

{'step': 2, 'action': 'Load content into the offscreen container', 'detail': 'Fetch or render new content (e.g., live feed items, product listings) into the offscreen container without triggering layout recalculation in the visible viewport'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Display a user notification', 'detail': "Overlay a notice (e.g., 'Scroll to top' button, banner) in the visible viewport to inform the user that new content is available"}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Enable user-initiated navigation', 'detail': 'Allow the user to click the notification or scroll to view the new content on demand'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Verify no layout shift in current viewport', 'detail': 'Confirm that the offscreen loading and notification do not cause unexpected shifts in the currently visible content'}
triggers: New content (e.g., live feed updates, additional products) needs to be loaded
User should not be surprised by layout shifts
Content availability should be communicated without forcing immediate visibility
constraints: New content must be placed in an offscreen container (outside visible viewport)
A user-facing notification must be displayed (e.g., button, banner)
No layout shift should occur in the currently visible viewport
User must be able to navigate to new content on demand
cautions: Ensure the notification is discoverable and clear
Test that offscreen content does not trigger unintended side effects (e.g., scroll performance)
Verify that the notification remains accessible if the user scrolls or interacts with the page
output_contract: New content is loaded and ready offscreen; user notification is displayed and discoverable; no layout shift occurs in the current viewport; user can navigate to new content on demand without surprise or disruption.

examples.input: Live feed receives 5 new posts while user is reading current feed
examples.output: Posts are loaded offscreen; 'New posts available' notification appears at top of feed; user can tap notification to scroll to new posts; no layout shift in current view
examples.notes: Example from Twitter live feed pattern

examples.input: Product listing page loads additional items as user scrolls
examples.output: New products are loaded offscreen; 'Load more' or 'Scroll to top' button appears; user can click to view new products; current viewport remains stable

metadata.prompt: Load new content (e.g., live feed updates, additional products) in an offscreen container. Display a user-facing notification (e.g., 'Scroll to top' button) to inform the user that new content is ready. Ensure no layout shift occurs in the currently visible viewport. Allow the user to navigate to the new content on demand.
